title: Strict dg Yoneda embedding and the formal cone enlargement
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $\mathcal A$ be a small $R$-linear cochain dg category with signed Leibniz composition as in [lem-coef-dgcat-free-cell-calculus]. A right dg $\mathcal A$-module is a family of cochain complexes $M(z)$ with unital associative actions $M(y)\otimes_R\mathcal A(z,y)\to M(z)$ satisfying $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^{|m|}m\,d(a)$. A homogeneous module map of degree $n$ consists of degree-$n$ $R$-linear maps commuting with these right actions; its differential is $\partial q=d_Nq-(-1)^nq d_M$. Write $\mathrm{dgMod}(\mathcal A)$ for the dg category with these objects and morphism complexes. Composition is composition of the underlying graded maps. Put $h_x(z)=\mathcal A(z,x)$ with its composition action. For every right dg module $M$, evaluation at $1_x$ is an isomorphism of complexes $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{dgMod}(\mathcal A)}(h_x,M)\cong M(x)$, with inverse sending $m$ to the map $a\mapsto ma$.

There is a small dg category $\operatorname{Cone}(\mathcal A)$ whose labelled objects are all $h_x$ and, for each closed degree-zero $u:x\to y$, a labelled object $C_u$ represented by the right dg module $h_y\oplus h_x[1]$, with $h_x[1]^j=h_x^{j+1}$, the unchanged right graded action, and differential
$$D_u=\begin{pmatrix}d_{h_y}&u\circ-\\ 0&-d_{h_x}\end{pmatrix}.$$
Its morphism complexes consist of all homogeneous module maps between these objects, with the differential above. The embedding $\mathcal A\to\operatorname{Cone}(\mathcal A)$, $x\mapsto h_x$, identifies every original morphism complex with the corresponding morphism complex, preserving composition and units. In particular
$$\operatorname{Cone}(\mathcal A)(h_z,C_u)\cong\operatorname{Cone}\bigl(\mathcal A(z,x)\xrightarrow{u\circ-}\mathcal A(z,y)\bigr),$$
where $\operatorname{Cone}(v)^j=\mathcal A(z,y)^j\oplus\mathcal A(z,x)^{j+1}$ with differential $(a,b)\mapsto(da+vb,-db)$. The graded decomposition of $C_u$ gives degree-zero maps $\iota_y:h_y\to C_u$, $\pi_y:C_u\to h_y$, a degree-$-1$ map $\iota_x:h_x\to C_u$ and a degree-$1$ map $\pi_x:C_u\to h_x$. They satisfy $\pi_y\iota_y=1$, $\pi_x\iota_x=1$, $\pi_y\iota_x=\pi_x\iota_y=0$ and $\iota_y\pi_y+\iota_x\pi_x=1_{C_u}$ as graded maps; they need not be closed. A degree-$n$ map $C_u\to C_v$, for $v:x'\to y'$, is a matrix with entries in
$$\begin{pmatrix}\mathcal A(y,y')^n&\mathcal A(x,y')^{n-1}\\ \mathcal A(y,x')^{n+1}&\mathcal A(x,x')^n\end{pmatrix}.$$
Composition is matrix multiplication on the underlying graded modules and the differential is $M\mapsto D_vM-(-1)^nMD_u$. Every dg functor $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ extends to these small labelled cone categories, taking $h_x$ to $h_{F(x)}$, $C_u$ to $C_{F(u)}$, and applying $F$ to the matrix entries. These extensions preserve identities and composition of dg functors.

proof.text: The free-cell conventions give an R-linear dg category with cochain Hom complexes, associative composition, and the signed Leibniz rule. For right dg modules, graded module maps form complexes with differential ∂q=d_Nq-(-1)^nq d_M; the module action identities imply ∂²=0, and composition obeys the dg Leibniz rule. Thus the stated objects and morphism complexes form the dg category dgMod(A).

source.place: Chapter 1, §1.2, Definition 1.1, printed p. 25, and Example 1.2 / Definitions 1.3–1.4, printed p. 26; direct verification for graded right-module maps.

proof.text: For a homogeneous module map q:h_x→M of degree n, set m=q_x(1_x). Right-linearity forces q_z(a)=m a for every homogeneous a∈A(z,x), and the module action constructs a unique map from every homogeneous m∈M(x). Evaluating the differential of q at 1_x gives the differential of m, so evaluation is a bijection commuting with differentials and hence an isomorphism of complexes. Evaluation also sends composition with representable maps to the module action.

source.place: Chapter 1, §1.2, Definitions 1.3–1.4, printed p. 26 (module maps and representable Yoneda functor); the evaluation-at-identity calculation is supplied explicitly here by the agent, rather than quoted as a calculation printed in the source.

proof.text: For each closed degree-zero u:x→y, the shifted direct sum h_y⊕h_x[1] with the displayed action and differential D_u is a right dg module: the off-diagonal terms in D_u² cancel because du=0. Take labels h_x for all x and one label C_u for each such u; this is a small set because A is small and each Hom complex is small. The full dg subcategory on these modules is Cone(A). The Yoneda calculation identifies the Hom complex between h_x and h_y with A(x,y), so x↦h_x is a dg embedding preserving units and composition.

source.place: Chapter 1, §1.3, proof of Proposition 1.7, printed p. 27 (cone module and differential), and §1.3.1, proof of Lemma 1.10, printed p. 29 (full representable/cone subcategory); labelled small-category version checked directly.

proof.text: A homogeneous map between the two-term direct sums is determined by its four component maps. Accounting for the shift h_x[1]^j=h_x^{j+1} places a degree-n map C_u→C_v in the four Hom complexes A(y,y')^n, A(x,y')^{n-1}, A(y,x')^{n+1}, and A(x,x')^n. Matrix composition is ordinary graded composition of components, while the module-map differential is D_vM-(-1)^nMD_u. Specializing the source to h_z and the target to C_u gives the displayed cone of A(z,x)→A(z,y), with differential (a,b)↦(da+ub,-db). The four coordinate inclusions and projections have the stated degrees and graded biproduct identities.

source.place: Chapter 1, §1.3, proof of Proposition 1.7, printed p. 27 (degree-minus-one matrix and commutator differential); general-degree and two-cone formulas checked directly by the agent.

proof.text: For a dg functor F:A→B, applying F to each representable action, closed arrow label, and matrix component preserves module-linearity, differentials, identities, and composition. It therefore sends h_x to h_{F(x)} and C_u to C_{F(u)}, defining a dg functor Cone(A)→Cone(B); the construction is compatible with composition of dg functors because every component is obtained by applying F entrywise.

source.place: Chapter 1, §1.3.1, proof of Lemma 1.10, printed p. 29 (extension to the representable/cone subcategory); simultaneous labelled cone functoriality checked directly entrywise.
